subject: Re: EmberForge dedicated capacity — compute fallback & hedge plan
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina@emberforge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — EmberForge production expectations

Hi Irene / Kim,

Thanks again for the demo last week. EmberForge is ready to move from pilot to a committed Dedicated environment, and we need a sizing recommendation and a short hedging/fallback plan for procurement. High-level profile below:

- Workloads: conversational assistant (primary) and some batched reranking jobs (secondary).
- Traffic profile: expected peak concurrent active users ~600 during US business hours; peak request spike observed in pilot up to ~12 requests/sec sustained for ~2-3 minutes.
- Request composition (pilot telemetry attached in emberforge_token_profile.csv): average prompt tokens 80, average completion tokens 120 (so avg ~200 tokens per request).
- SLOs: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 350 ms for conversational flows; lower priority for reranking (p95 <= 1.5s acceptable).
- Durability: must have predictable capacity during business hours; early-morning bursts can be tolerated if fallback invoked.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Based on the attached token profile, what committed GPU footprint do you recommend to meet the p95 350ms target at peak?
2) What conservative headroom % do you recommend for a 12-month commit (to avoid SLA breaches during growth/burst)?
3) If we need to degrade gracefully, what model downgrade / routing fallback would you propose (latency vs quality tradeoff)?

Please include a short note on autoscaling limits and warm cache strategies—we want minimal cold-start exposure.

Thanks,
Lina Park
VP Product, EmberForge



From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina@emberforge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — EmberForge production expectations

Lina — thanks for the clear profile and the CSV. I ran a quick capacity sketch with our inference benchmarks and here is a pragmatic recommendation + fallback strategy you can take to procurement. Attachment: EF-dedicated-proposal-draft.pdf (summary + cost sketch).

Summary of compute math (short):
- Peak tokens/sec = peak requests/sec * avg tokens/request = 12 req/s * 200 tokens = 2,400 tokens/sec peak.
- Model we benchmarked in pilot: redwood-70b-quant (4-bit q4x) used as baseline for quality target. On H100 80GB (optimized kernels, live batching), a single GPU sustained throughput for sampling workloads similar to yours is ~300 tokens/sec (p95 per-token latency and system overhead included in the benchmark).
- Baseline GPUs needed = ceil(2,400 / 300) = 8 GPUs.
- Recommended committed slab = 12 H100 GPUs (x1.5 baseline) to provide ~40% headroom for short spikes, background batch jobs, and to keep buffering for autoscaling latency. That maps to 3 hosts (4 GPUs/host) for isolation and failure domain.

Latency fit notes:
- With the baseline 8-GPU mapping and aggressive batching disabled for interactive flows, our sim shows p95 generation = ~310 ms (model-only inference + network/turn overhead trimmed). That meets your 350 ms SLO but leaves little margin under real-world jitter.
- With the recommended 12-GPU reserved slab, expected p95 under the same load drops to ~240–280 ms (additional headroom to absorb bursty increases and model warmup phases).

Fallback / graceful degradation options:
1) Model downgrade: route to redwood-35b-quant (q4) variant under sustained overload. Per-GPU throughput for 35B on H100 in our tests is ~540 tokens/sec, so an equivalent capacity using 35B would need ~5 GPUs to handle the 2,400 tokens/sec baseline. Quality drop is measurable on longer completions — we can toggle only for non-critical flows.
2) Quantized variant + packing: we can offer a heavily quantized 70B q2 variant which increases tokens/sec per GPU to ~420, but expect hallucination/regression risk on some prompts. Use as a last-resort fallback for short bursts.
3) Routing by priority: keep conversational traffic pinned to baseline slab; route lower-priority reranking and batch requests to lower-cost preemptible capacity or to a queued offline path.

Autoscaling and cache warm-up:
- Autoscaling: set conservative upper bound = 3 hosts (12 GPUs) for reserved capacity and a burst policy that allows 2x temporary burst to on-demand capacity for <15 minutes with a fallback trigger at 60% sustained utilization for 3 minutes.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache for common prompts. Warm caches reduce per-request token work by up to ~30% in our telemetry for similar customers; we recommend a scheduled warmup window before your peak hours to pre-populate hot prefixes.

Next steps / asks from EmberForge:
- Confirm whether the 40% headroom aligns with procurement appetite (we can simulate 25% vs 40% scenarios and run cost deltas).
- Do you want the fallback to be automatic (system-initiated) or manual (Ops triggered)?
- Approve the attached draft and we’ll generate a DocuSign-ready proposal.

I can jump on a 30-min call later this week to walk the numbers with your SRE/infra team.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Inference Sizing & Operations
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0141

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Lina Park <lina@emberforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — EmberForge production expectations

Quick clarifying questions before we lock a sizing commitment: Lina —
1) Is the 12 req/s spike uniform (all ~200-token requests) or does it include a distribution with some shorter 30–50 token quick checks? Shorter completions materially increase tokens/sec headroom but reduce per-request latency pressure.
2) For the reranking batch jobs: are they latency-sensitive during business hours or can they be scheduled to non-peak windows? If they run during peaks, they should be throttled to background gradient so they don't consume the slab.

Operationally, we should also decide the fallback mode: automatic fallback gives you a smoother user experience at the expense of a small quality delta if we downgrade models automatically. Manual fallback is safer but requires an on-call workflow and runbook. Our recommendation (from an ops perspective) is automatic fallback with a strict quality-guard set (route only requests that match a conservative prompt fingerprint).

Also attaching a short cost-sensitivity sketch (compute_hedge_chart.png) that Irene and Ben prepared.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina@emberforge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — EmberForge production expectations

Lina — thanks for the quick answers on the call today. Summarizing agreed action items and the final pragmatic recommendation so procurement can move forward:

Agreed facts from the call:
- Peak shape: 12 req/s spike is primarily the 200-token conversational flows; ~20% of the traffic are short 40–60 token checks which provide slight headroom.
- Reranking jobs will be rate-limited during peak hours and scheduled where possible to off-peak.
- EmberForge prefers automatic fallback with a conservative fingerprint routing as Karthik recommended.

Final recommendation (for contract):
- Commitment: 12 H100 GPUs (reserved Dedicated slab) — maps to 3 hosts x 4 GPUs. This meets the p95 350 ms SLO with ~40% operational headroom.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to redwood-35b-quant for non-critical sessions when slab utilization > 85% for 90s. System will mark requests as downgraded in the audit log for quality regression tracking.
- Autoscale/burst: allow 2x short burst to on-demand capacity for up to 15 minutes; after that, throttles + fallback engaged.
- Cache: enable prefix cache and schedule warmup starting 30 minutes before expected business peak. Expected cache benefit ~20–30% tokens saved on hot flows.

Deliverables we will send by end of day:
- Final commitment proposal (PDF) + a one-sheet explaining the fallback quality tradeoffs (EF-dedicated-proposal-draft.pdf).
- DocuSign-ready attachment and HubSpot record updated (links above).

Please confirm and we’ll push the procurement package. If all good, Ben will draft the MSA addendum for the Dedicated slab and Kimberly will run the final SLA check.

Thanks — looking forward to getting EmberForge onto Dedicated.

—Irene
Director, Inference Sizing & Operations, Redwood Inference
